newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Protesting S.Korean students fast for fifth day.
newsitem.headline: Protesting S.Korean students fast for fifth day.

text.p: Radical South Korean students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam sweltered under the blazing sun on Monday during the fifth day of a hunger strike outside a Seoul cathedral, witnesses said.

About 20 students, who chained themselves to a rail on the grounds of Myongdong Cathedral in central Seoul last Thursday, also called for an end to the government crackdown on what they called their "democratic student movement".

Hundreds of police ringed the grounds of the Roman Catholic church to prevent other students joining the protest, the witnesses said. The cathedral is a traditional sanctuary for anti-government protesters.

The hunger strikers are members of the pro-North Korean Hanchongryon student body that the government banned last week after a police officer was killed during riots organised by the group earlier this month.
Police said the group had also beat two men to death during questioning aimed at extracting confessions that they were police spies.
Ten other Hanchongryon members who started the hunger strike on Thursday quit the protest over the weekend after emotional pleas from their parents, witnesses said.
They said the protesters were drinking water with salt and covered themselves with towels to ward off the scorching sun.
The Hanchongryon has admitted responsibility for the death of a suspected police informer, Lee Suk, in Seoul.
It also has confessed to beating another suspected police informer, Lee Jong-kwon, who was found dead last month in Chunnam National University in the southern city of Kwangju.
Police have made several arrests in connection with both cases.
The militant student group has called for the reunification of the Korean peninsula under a formula suggested by communist North Korea. Government officials say the group takes orders from Pyongyang.
Student councils from 116 universities across South Korea are affiliated with the Hanchongryon. None have publicly renounced their link since the organisation was banned.
